_comment: The per-beat transition rules BOTH languages must enforce (D89). A beat's transition_out overrides the style pack's default for the junction it OWNS — the one to the next beat — so it has to be checked against the same allow-list the compiler and the renderer will read. The worker's validate_beat_sheet and the platform's editor route apply this table through worker/tests/test_validators.py and platform/test/transitionRules.test.ts, so the two cannot drift. Each case is a two-beat sheet: `transition_out` goes on the FIRST beat (the one that hands over), and `allowed_transitions` is the video's style pack list, defaulting to ["cut", "crossfade"] when a case does not name one. `expect` is a substring that must appear in some violation; an empty list means the beats must be accepted.
script: The port fed the capital. Nearly 70% of all grain passed through it.

cases.name: a transition the style pack allows is accepted
a hard cut is nameable like any other, when the pack allows it
no transition at all: the beat takes the pack's default
a transition the style pack does not allow
a pack that allows it accepts what another pack refuses
a kind that is not a transition at all is refused by the schema
an empty allow-list is not a rule — the pack is what is wrong, not the beat

_pack_comment: D95 — the rules on the style pack's transitions block itself, beyond what the schema can say: every kind a mix, section break or duration names must be allowed, and a share needs a mix to fill it. Each case is a `transitions` block; `expect` is a substring some problem must contain, [] means accepted. Asserted by worker/tests/test_transitions.py and platform/test/transitionRules.test.ts.

pack_cases.name: a pack with no D95 fields is what every pack was
a share with an allowed mix
a share with nothing to fill it
a mix kind the pack does not allow
a section break the pack does not allow
a duration for a kind the pack does not allow
the default must still be allowed
a mix with no share is inert, not wrong
